title: Why the Pomodoro technique really works

scenes.narration: This study trick works... but not for the reason you think.
It's the Pomodoro technique. Twenty-five minutes of work, then a five minute break.
People say it works because the breaks recharge your brain.
Nice idea. But that's not the main reason.
The hardest part of studying is starting. An essay feels huge, so you grab your phone.
But twenty-five minutes? Easy. The timer shrinks the task until starting isn't scary.
And once you've started, you usually keep going.
So set a timer, do one round, and tick it off.

source.citation: Cirillo, F. (2006). The Pomodoro Technique. Self-published; later editions by Currency (2018).
source.finding: Describes the 25-minute work / 5-minute break method. It is a practitioner's method, not a research finding.
source.caveat: The script's claim that the method works mainly by making it easier to start is a plausible argument, not an established result. Controlled studies of the technique itself are few and small.
